_about: Every book of text hung on the ayahs, and the only place any of them is named.
Adding a book is an entry here plus its file in downloads/, then:
python backend/scripts/import_quran_editions.py --only <id>
No code is written to add a book. That is the point of this file.
kind        tafsir | translation. Decides which panel shows it.
short       what the book is called in the picker, where seven full titles
would be a wall of text. The full name stays on the credit line.
language    ar | en. Decides which way the text reads and how it is folded.
format      which foreign shape the file is, and so which reader opens it:
ayah-json        one text per ayah, written by fetch_quran_editions.py
qul-tafsir       the tafsir table of a QUL sqlite export
qul-translation  the translation(s) table of a QUL sqlite export
app-tafsir-db    this app's own tafsir.db, from build_quran_tafsir.py
file        relative to backend/data/quran/. Rename the download to match.
fetch       where a book with no file yet can be downloaded from, no account
needed. Only ayah-json books have one:
python backend/scripts/fetch_quran_editions.py --only <id>
mirror is tafsir-api or quran.com; book is that mirror's own name
for it. A book with no fetch block is acquired by hand.
origin      where the text came from, so a passage can be traced back.
licence     what the publisher actually states. Not what we assume.
credit      which entry in data/sources.json says how far to trust it.
confidence  verified | translated. The badge the reader sees. Every book here is
a published human work, so every book here is verified. "translated"
means a machine made the English, which is true of no book in this
file; showing it beside Saheeh International said the opposite.
index       whether Daleel searches inside this book. Every commentary
here is now searched; the only books left out are the two
English translations that render ayahs Saheeh International
already carries. Changing it takes TWO runs, because the
flag is copied into library.db at import time and the
search index is built from the copy, not from this file:
python backend/scripts/import_quran_editions.py
python backend/scripts/build_daleel_index.py
Doing only the second leaves the search exactly as it was,
with no error to say so.
One English translation is searched, not all three. They render the same 6,236
ayahs, so indexing every one of them would answer each search three times over
with the same ayah. Saheeh International is the one indexed; the others are
read, not searched.
The books below are QUL's and Quran.com's. QUL's own download button needs a
free account, so a script cannot reach it; the same resources are mirrored
openly by spa5k/tafsir_api, and that is what `fetch` uses. Downloading a QUL
sqlite by hand still works: put it in downloads/ and set format to qul-tafsir.
Either way nothing is fetched while the app is running.
